metadata.name: yes
metadata.description: Output a string repeatedly until killed

installation.note: yes is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: yes prints a string (default 'y') repeatedly, one per line, until killed. It is often used to pipe into a command that prompts for confirmation (e.g., yes | apt install ...), or to generate repeated input for testing.
when_to_use: Generate repeated input for scripts or tests
Stress test or fill a pipe (yes something)

syntax.description: Without STRING, yes prints 'y' forever. With STRING, it prints that string (one line per iteration) until killed.

examples.title: Auto-confirm install
examples.description: Pipe 'y' to apt so it does not prompt (use with care)
examples.use_case: Non-interactive install when you want default yes

common_pitfalls.description: yes never stops on its own; it will fill pipes and use CPU.
common_pitfalls.solution: Always kill it (Ctrl+C) or pipe to a command that consumes and then exits.
